title: KV view-pin linger and multipool ownership provenance investigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Production and soak tests show a gradual GPU RSS increase over multi-hour continuous-batching workloads. Unlike prior slab-residency regressions, this leak surface correlates with KV cache 'view pin' objects that outlive expected ownership windows and prevent allocator arenas from returning pages to cudaMallocAsync. Hypothesis: under high-frequency batch handoffs, a race between stream-epoch advance and multipool ownership reclamation leaves a small set of pages marked live by stale view references, causing resident growth over time.

What we've observed:
- Reproducer (batcher-sim v3) ramps to 4k rps with mixed sequence lengths. Resident GPU memory increases ~120MB/hour on a 80GB GPU under these conditions.
- nvprof / nvidia-smi show stable allocation counts but rising RSS. Heap snapshots (gpu-heap-snap-YYYYMMDD) show ~2–8 pinned pages per outstanding key slice that do not transition to free.
- Traces show EPOCH advancement logs (epoch=1234 -> epoch=1235) but corresponding view-pin destructors do not run until a later stream callback. Under contention the delayed callback can be tens of seconds.
- Enabling synchronous cudaFree on the reclaim path stops the leak in repro but adds ~4% p99 latency.

Reproducer and how to run:
- repo: internal/tools/batcher-sim (branch: kv-viewpin-repro)
- command: ./run_repro --mode=continuous --gpu=0 --seq-dist=mixed --rps=4000 --duration=3h
- artifact: logs and heap snapshots produced to /tmp/kv_viewpin_repro_*

Initial diagnosis steps taken:
1) Added instrumentation to KV view lifecycle to emit owner_id, stream_id, epoch_when_created, epoch_when_released.
2) Correlated view-pin lifetimes with stream callbacks: many view pins are released only after an asynchronous post-batch cleanup callback which is queued on the batch completion stream. When the stream's event is not yet processed (work queued on same stream), the callback is deferred and the view remains live.
3) Reproduced in minimal harness by artificially delaying the stream callback consumer, reproducing the leak quickly.
4) Verified allocator (cudaMallocAsync) arenas hold onto pages because the memory is still referenced by a live view object. Because the runtime uses multi-pool arenas, page ownership metadata gets partitioned and some pools were not eligible for instant coalescing, increasing fragmentation.

Files collected / artifacts:
- gpu-heap-snap-2026-03-09-11.tgz (heap HWM diffs)
- kv-view-lifetimes-2026-03-10.log (instrumentation trace)
- batcher-sim-v3-repro.tar.gz (reproducer scripts and config)
- flamegraphs: p99-latency-epoch-reconcile.svg

Proposed workstreams and experiments:
A) Short-term mitigation (low-risk): change reclaim path to use epoch checkpointing + opportunistic host-thread draining on long-pending callbacks. This reduces leak observed in repro without changing async free semantics. Tradeoff: increases CPU housekeeping and complexity.
B) Medium-term fix (target runtime-1.22): adopt lightweight reference-queue where views post their finalizer to a dedicated reclamation thread that guarantees ordering with epoch advancement. This removes dependency on the CUDA stream callback for ownership release while preserving async frees.
C) Long-term improvement: revise multipool ownership metadata to track page provenance and allow cross-pool coalescing when a page set is entirely unpinned. This will reduce fragmentation and make bulk cudaMallocAsync returns more likely.

Immediate actions completed:
- Created reproducible harness and added instrumentation (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3254).
- Ran bisection across allocator changes since 1.20; no single commit fully regressed behavior — appears to be an interaction between view lifetime change (ENG-92812-era) and multipool coalescer heuristics.

Open tasks / next steps: 
- Implement the reclamation-thread prototype (spike branch: eng/kv-reclaim-thread) and run 72-hour soak across 10 nodes. (Assigned)
- Add unit + integration tests that simulate delayed stream callbacks and assert no resident growth.
- Measure CPU overhead and p99 cost of host-thread draining mitigation.
- Run additional experiments with reduced deferred-free threshold (configurable knob) to see tradeoffs.

Blocking / dependencies:
- Needs a predictable testbed with deterministic stream scheduling (infra ticket: ENG-102120) to validate at scale.
- May need consult from CUDA experts if we change cudaMallocAsync usage patterns (cc: Emily Chen).

Customer impact: medium. Production clusters using continuous-batching saw gradual memory growth requiring periodic node drains; no immediate OOM in deployed fleets yet but sustained workloads could approach capacity over weeks.

Release target: runtime-1.22 for medium-term fix, with short-term mitigation as a hotfix if soak confirms CPU cost acceptable.

Related tickets and references: [ENG-21388, ENG-31500, ENG-36142]
